items.title: These 3 Agentic AI Stocks Have More Than Hype Behind Their Growth Stories
items.summary: ServiceNow, UiPath, and Palo Alto Networks show real agentic AI traction through earnings growth, enterprise adoption, and partnerships, making their fundamentals worth watching amid market volatility.

items.title: How Low Can UiPath Stock Go When Its Numbers Are Not The Problem?
items.summary: UiPath (PATH) trades at about $14, some 29% below its high of the past year, and it has lost 11.7% over the past month. Its results are not what did that. The fall is recent: the stock is still up 34.5% over the past three months, and over the past twelve months it returned 18.9% against 17.0% for the S&P 500. What matters is how far a stock like this falls in a real shock.

items.title: Why Salesforce’s Homegrown AI Model Won’t Move the Stock Until 2027
items.summary: Salesforce just unveiled Koa, its first homegrown AI model built for CRM reasoning, but a gap between launch and availability raises a pointed question: can a model nobody can buy yet actually move the stock?

items.title: ServiceNow Stock Leads 3 Large Cap Growth Names Facing Higher Rate Pressure
items.summary: Federal debt crossing US$40b has turned the spotlight on Washington’s balance sheet and on how higher perceived sovereign risk could ripple through everything you own. This is not just a bond story. Equities tied to growth, pricing power, and strong balance sheets may react very differently as investors reassess inflation and discount rates. items.title: Would You Want CRM Stock Back At The Price It Just Left?
items.summary: Salesforce (CRM) trades near $250 a share, close to its 52-week high after a fast three-month run. Selling a put pays you now for agreeing to buy it much lower later, and you keep the payment either way. The catch: you only want this if you would be glad to own Salesforce at that lower price. The open part of that answer is how much its new agent products can actually be charged for.

items.title: The Palantir Question Nobody Can Answer Yet: How Big Can This Get?
items.summary: Palantir is posting growth numbers that make every enterprise software peer look slow, yet the stock has gone nowhere for a year. Understanding why reveals something uncomfortable about what fair value actually means for a company this unusual.
